newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks Syrian durum as debt repayment.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks Syrian durum as debt repayment.

text.p: Syria may pay its $14 million debt to Bulgaria in durum wheat deliveries, Bulgaria's trade minister said on Tuesday.
"The possibilities for paying back Syria's debt are very limited. The only solution is paying the debt by durum wheat imports," Daniela Bobeva told journalists.
She added that the two countries were expected to sign a trade agreement.
Syria owes $10 million to Bulgaria's biggest commercial bank, Bulbank, and $4 million to the state-owned food trading company Hranexport.
Earlier talks on such a deal between the Syrians and Bulgaria's former Socialist government collapsed, banking sources said.
A new cabinet will take office this month following elections on April 19 which gave a majority to the reformist Union of Democratic Forces.
Bulgaria, suffering a severe economic crisis, has been seeking ways to secure repayment of some of the debts contracted during the communist era, which include more than $1 billion owed by Iraq.
